root_motivation: A tenant owner who wants a friend to use their tool has to run a relay protocol across two humans and two agents: five steps, two of them out of band, and a per-IP signup cap that fails a group of friends in one room. Grounding incident: Joe 2026-10-01 asked "how can I share this new mcp server with friends?" and the best available answer was signup(handoff: true) -> host.redeem -> carry tenant_key -> host.whoami -> paste a tenant id -> Joe runs host.tool_share/host.share_caller_limit per friend. mcphost already has every primitive an invite link needs (path-authenticated routes, session binding, shares by tenant id, consent rows, one-time claim tokens) and no link.
user_persona: Joe, a tenant owner who wants to text one URL to a friend so their agent can read a shared tool with no other step; the friend's agent, which pastes the URL and keeps the tenant it is handed; five friends on one wifi joining the same invite within an hour; an agent relaying a shared-tool result to another agent, which needs its own invite link in hand without a second call.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given inviter tenant A with a published tool t, When A calls host.invite.create share=["t"], Then the result has a url of the form /i/<code>/mcp, max_uses: 10, expires_at 30 days out, and host.invite.list shows it with uses: 0.

Given that URL, When a fresh session POSTs tools/call host.tool_call {name: "<A ns>.t"} with no header, Then a new tenant B is created with source: "invite:<code>", the call succeeds, the response carries onboarding.url, onboarding.invited_by, and onboarding.shared_tools: ["t"], and uses is 1.
Given tenant B, When host.agent.contacts is called from A and from B, Then each lists the other as accepted with via: "invite:<code>", and host.usage by=caller tool=t on A shows B's call.
Given an invite with max_uses: 2 and two concurrent first calls from two fresh sessions plus a third, When they race, Then exactly two tenants are created and the third receives invite_invalid.
Given a revoked or expired code, When any request hits /i/<code>/mcp, Then HTTP 404 invite_invalid, the browser page reveals no inviter identity, and existing invitees' shares still work.

Given six fresh sessions from one IP joining via one invite within an hour, When each makes its first call, Then all six succeed (per-code limiter, not per-IP) and a 21st within the hour is refused with invite_rate_limited.

Given a free-plan tenant with 3 live invites already created, When it calls host.invite.create again, Then it is refused with invites_quota_exceeded; When one existing invite is revoked, Then a new create succeeds.
Live/production deployment evidence that invite-created tenants and standing invites behave correctly against prod.
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: Live/prod deployment evidence; needs a real deploy and operator authorization this coding sandbox does not have.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every tenant is born with a standing invite (kind: "standing", no expiry, no max_uses, share: []); host.whoami returns invite_url; the standing invite does not count toward the live-invites cap.
Standing invites are rate-limited per code (20 creations/hour) and per inviter (100/day); host.invite.revoke on a standing invite rotates it (a new URL is issued) rather than deleting it.
host.agent.lookup returns invited_by and invitees_count for a tenant's lineage; host.usage gains invites: {sent_7d, accepted_7d, k}.

Shares are one hop: tools shared to an invitee by an invite are visible to that invitee only; an invitee's own standing invite shares nothing by default, and an invitee cannot re-share a tool it does not own, across an invite chain of depth 3.
The result of a shared-tool call made by an invitee carries _meta.invite_url of the invitee's own standing invite once per session (first shared call only).

scope: src/invites.rs (new): host.invite.create/list/revoke business logic, invite_url, invite_path_code, claim_on_first_call (the narrow implicit-signup-on-/i/{code}/mcp mechanism), mint_standing_invite, InviteHintTracker (once-per-session _meta.invite_url hint).

src/db.rs: invites/invite_joins tables (migrations/0067_invite_links.sql, 0068_standing_invite_code.sql), InviteRow/ClaimedInvite/InvitesUsage7d, is_live vs is_connectable liveness split, create_invite/claim_invite (atomic BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction)/revoke_invite/list_invites_for_tenant/invite_lineage/invites_usage_7d, tenants.invited_by_tenant_id, contacts.via.

src/handler.rs: host.invite.create/list/revoke Tool descriptors and dispatch arms; call_tool's Auth::Anonymous + /i/{code}/mcp claim gate; _meta.invite_url hint attachment alongside the existing alias-deprecation _meta.
src/http.rs: require_live_invite_code middleware and the /i/{code}/mcp router (mirrors require_known_url_secret/url_mcp_router).
src/control.rs: signup() mints a standing invite at tenant birth; whoami() returns invite_url; usage() returns invites: {sent_7d, accepted_7d, k}.

Necessary fallout (registry grew by 3 tools, no removals): docs/tools.md, www/llms.txt, contracts/host-tools.v1.json regenerated; tests/toolname_ac08_tools_list_counts_updated.rs and tests/compat_ac04_ac05_admin_and_tenant_cache_fields.rs tool-count literals updated 175->178; tests/callerusage_ac06_no_by_shape_unchanged.rs's host.usage no-by field set gained "invites".
non_goals: Inviting into an existing tenant (multi-user tenants); every invitee is a new tenant.
Human account linking or billing attachment for invitees (/claim unchanged).
Wildcard public shares; invites are targeted.
Requirement 8 (www/index.html "Invite a friend" section) and requirement 9 (invite-carries-a-channel) -- P1/P2, no AC in this dispatch's assigned list.
AC8 (prod/live deployment evidence) -- operator-provisioned, not reachable from this coding sandbox.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_invite: test_prefix invite (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/invite_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build claim_on_first_call as a route-scoped mechanism in src/invites.rs rather than a crate-wide 'anonymous call implicit-signs-up' feature?
five_whys_trace.a: This PRD's own Depends-on names PRD-mcphost-implicit-signup's mechanism, but no generic anonymous-call-creates-a-tenant path exists anywhere else in handler.rs; building it crate-wide would be new surface no other route asks for. Scoping it to Auth::Anonymous on /i/{code}/mcp is the minimal mechanism that satisfies requirement 2, and Db::claim_invite binds the session before returning so every later call on that session resolves through the ordinary session-binding step instead (requirement 6).

five_whys_trace.q: Why split db::is_live (full liveness incl. max_uses exhaustion) from db::is_connectable (revoked/expired only) instead of one liveness check?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4's race test needs request #3 to receive invite_invalid from the atomic claim itself, not a timing-dependent 404 from route middleware checking max_uses against a count that two concurrent transactions are still racing to increment; AC5 only tests revoked/expired at the route layer. One shared full-liveness check would make AC4 flaky depending on which of the three requests the middleware happens to schedule last.

five_whys_trace.q: Why add a nullable invites.code_plain column instead of hashing every invite code at rest like every other secret in this crate?
five_whys_trace.a: host.whoami must return the SAME invite_url on every call for a standing invite (unlike a one-time-reveal secret), which requires the plaintext code to be retrievable after creation; code_plain is populated only for kind='standing' rows, a deliberate, documented departure from the hash-at-rest convention rather than a blanket exception.

five_whys_trace.q: Why implement AC12's one-hop sharing via a dedicated per-invite SQLite group rather than new enforcement code?
five_whys_trace.a: tools.visibility/tools.shared_group already support only one group per tool; a per-invite group (__invite_{invite_id}) that only promotes a currently-private tool to group visibility (never touching an already-shared tool) gives one-hop sharing for free, since a sub-invitee is never added to the original inviter's group -- the AC needed a proving fixture, not new mechanism.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is InviteHintTracker (AC13's once-per-session _meta.invite_url hint) an in-memory Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>> instead of a DB-backed dedup?
five_whys_trace.a: Same posture as session_bind.rs's own SessionBindings -- a hint is a UX nudge for an agent relaying a result to another agent, not state anything else in this crate reads or that needs to survive a restart; a DB table for it would be new durable surface this PRD's requirements don't ask for.

ambiguities_resolved.question: via_tenant_key_arg's name suggests 'a tenant_key argument was supplied', used as a gate condition alongside Auth::Anonymous for the /i/{code}/mcp claim path -- is that the right guard?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No: via_tenant_key_arg actually means 'no Authorization header was present' (true for every header-less request), so gating the claim on !via_tenant_key_arg made it never fire. Fixed by gating on matches!(auth, Auth::Anonymous) alone.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does onboarding.url / invite_url return an absolute URL or a bare path?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Absolute, matching this codebase's established state.public_url-prefixed convention (same as /u/new's own URL field).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the route-level 404 for a dead invite code also cover max_uses exhaustion, same as revoked/expired?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- scoped strictly to revoked/expired (db::is_connectable); max_uses exhaustion is checked only inside the atomic claim (db::is_live), to keep AC4's race deterministic rather than timing-dependent on route middleware.
